b: May cause tremors, poor feeding and seizures, and make hypocalcaemia difficult to correct. Measure magnesium and calcium; replace magnesium according to neonatal protocol and monitor renal function.

snip.t: The electrolyte derangements are hypophosphataemia, hypomagnesaemia and hypokalaemia.

snip.t: | Serum potassium & magnesium | Identifies pro-arrhythmic electrolyte states | Hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia predisposes to Torsades/VT |

Underlying cause correction: Treat severe malaria, manage sepsis, correct hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia, discontinue QT-prolonging medicines (e.g., macrolides, fluoroquinolones, haloperidol), and treat underlying TB pericarditis or ischaemia.

Hypocalcaemia: Vitamin D deficiency, hypoparathyroidism, renal failure, acute pancreatitis, massive transfusion — HIV‑related malabsorption, TB meningitis (calcitonin dysregulation), chronic diarrhoea, malaria‑induced hypomagnesaemia
| Hypocalcaemia | Post‑surgical neck, vitamin D deficiency, hypomagnesaemia, CKD | Low ionised Ca²⁺, prolonged QT, positive Chvostek |
Hypomagnesaemia: may contribute to arrhythmia and refractory hypokalaemia.
